statements.appliesTo: social workers, and so those qualifying
statements.about: equipped for complexity and able to lead change
statements.paraphrase: Because the work takes place amid uncertainty, complexity and ambiguity, social workers must have the knowledge and skills to cope with it; they are also expected to take a critical part in debate about what the profession is for and to show they can analyse, adjust to, manage and in time lead change.

forPractitioner.text: Courses prepare students for settings marked by uncertainty and ambiguity: social workers must hold the knowledge and skills these demand, and are expected to debate the purpose of the profession critically and to show they can handle and eventually lead change.

forBeneficiary.text: As a social worker you must be ready for situations that are uncertain, complex and unclear. You will be expected to question what social work is for and to show you can make sense of change, adapt to it, manage it and, later on, lead it.

statements.appliesTo: course providers
statements.about: duty to make reasonable adjustments
statements.paraphrase: Course providers carry a duty to adjust reasonably for students so the learning environment is accessible to everyone, those with protected characteristics included, in keeping with the IFSW principles of justice, rights, shared responsibility and respect for difference.

forPractitioner.text: Make reasonable adjustments so that every student, including those with protected characteristics, can learn in an accessible setting; the statement ties this duty to the profession's own principles as well as to law.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Social Work degree

statements.appliesTo: course providers and practice placements
statements.about: legal duty to adjust, on courses and placements
statements.paraphrase: Both course providers and practice placements hold a legal duty to adjust reasonably so the learning environment is open and accessible to all students, including those with protected characteristics; QAA guidance on inclusive subject communities gives more.

forPractitioner.text: The legal duty to make reasonable adjustments reaches placements as well as the university: agree with placement partners how adjustments made on campus carry over into practice settings.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider and placements; the student meets its effect

statements.appliesTo: course providers
statements.about: anticipatory reasonable adjustments in every setting
statements.paraphrase: Courses can be built to accommodate individual needs with access designed in, and providers are expected to make adjustments in advance to teaching, learning and assessment, on campus, online and in practice, so that every student can reach and show the intended outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Anticipate adjustments rather than waiting for requests, across campus, online and practice settings, so that all students can meet and evidence the outcomes; build accessibility into the curriculum itself.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: an expectation of the provider; the student meets its effect

statements.appliesTo: course providers
statements.about: procedures for authenticity and integrity with generative AI
statements.paraphrase: AI, generative AI included, now shapes society and practice; students and social workers engage with it critically to support people in line with social work values, providers can help them use it competently, critically, lawfully and ethically, and procedures will be in place to protect authenticity and academic integrity.

forPractitioner.text: Have procedures that protect authenticity and academic integrity where students use generative AI, and support students to use these tools competently, critically, lawfully and ethically for the good of people and communities.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: an expectation of the provider; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Social Work degree

statements.appliesTo: students and educators
statements.about: navigating technologies and their risks
statements.paraphrase: Technologies are met in many places and at many scales, with unequal access; students and educators need to handle them from varied angles, keep up with change and use them to improve learning, research and practice, while recognising and challenging the harm and discrimination they can create.

forPractitioner.text: Staff and students alike need to keep pace with changing technologies, use them to strengthen learning and practice, and recognise and challenge the risks and discrimination they can bring for individuals and groups.

forBeneficiary.text: You need to be able to find your way around changing technologies from different points of view, keep up to date, use them to help your learning and practice, and notice and push back on the harm or unfairness they can cause.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Social Work degree

statements.appliesTo: students and educators
statements.about: values guide technology; it never replaces relationships
statements.paraphrase: Social work values are expected to steer how students and staff use technology throughout learning, and technology and digital options should not stand in for human relationships or contact.

forPractitioner.text: Expect values to steer every use of technology in the course, and keep digital options from replacing the human contact that the profession depends on.

forBeneficiary.text: You are expected to let social work values guide how you use technology, and to make sure digital tools never take the place of real human relationships with the people you work with.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses
statements.about: ethics and dilemmas as a core requirement
statements.paraphrase: Social work education rests on values and ethics that ask practitioners to respect individual dignity yet also to take and carry out hard decisions, liberty included, where benefit and harm are both possible; courses therefore require the study, use of and critical reflection on ethical principles and dilemmas, which the regulators of all four nations reflect.

forPractitioner.text: Make ethical principles and professional dilemmas a core, required part of the course: their study, their application and critical reflection on them, including decisions that restrict liberty.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on course design; the student-facing outcome is in 4.11 aa and 2.27

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: qualified social workers, and so those qualifying
statements.about: working within contested debate and leading change
statements.paraphrase: Social work changes with social, political and economic pressures and with policy and law; qualified social workers need to be ready to understand and work within argument over the profession's nature and purpose, and to analyse, adapt to, manage and finally lead change.

forPractitioner.text: Prepare students to work inside a contested profession: they need to grasp the debate about what social work is for and to build the capacity to handle change and, over time, lead it.

forBeneficiary.text: You need to understand that people disagree about what social work is for, be able to work within that debate, and build your ability to cope with change, manage it and eventually lead it.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses in Wales
statements.about: approval by Social Care Wales and the Welsh context
statements.paraphrase: In Wales, courses must have Social Care Wales approval; the professional requirements sit in its qualifications framework and the award draws on the National Occupational Standards, the Welsh code of practice for social care and this statement; degrees run through partnerships with local authority employers and must reflect current Welsh law, policy and regulation.

forPractitioner.text: For a Welsh course, secure Social Care Wales approval, meet its qualifications framework, deliver through partnership with local authority employers, and keep content current with Welsh legislation, social policy and regulation.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on the course in Wales; the student-facing rule is in 2.12

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work students in Wales
statements.about: registering with Social Care Wales and following its Code
statements.paraphrase: Students in Wales must register with Social Care Wales and show that they understand and keep to its Code of Professional Practice for Social Care, during their studies and on into practice.

forPractitioner.text: Students on Welsh courses must register with Social Care Wales and show they understand and follow its Code of Professional Practice while studying and after qualifying.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study in Wales, you must register with Social Care Wales and show that you understand its Code of Professional Practice and follow it, both while you study and once you qualify.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses in England
statements.about: approval by Social Work England against its standards
statements.paraphrase: In England, courses must have Social Work England approval, meeting its Education and Training Standards and producing graduates who can show they meet its Professional Standards; approved courses also reflect wider curriculum guidance and this statement, and the Professional Standards Authority oversees the regulator.

forPractitioner.text: For a course in England, secure Social Work England approval against the Education and Training Standards, and make sure graduates can evidence the Professional Standards; reflect the regulator's knowledge, skills and behaviours guidance too.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on the course in England; the student meets its effect at registration

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work students in Northern Ireland
statements.about: political violence and integrated care in Northern Ireland
statements.paraphrase: Northern Ireland's framework specification, written jointly by the regulator and the health department, gives one set of learning requirements and outcomes, with some particular to the region, where students are required to grasp how its political violence bears on their practice and to consider their place in integrated health and social care after conflict.

forPractitioner.text: On a Northern Ireland course, students are required to understand the effect of political violence on practice and their role in joined-up health and social care bodies in a society emerging from conflict.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study in Northern Ireland, you are required to understand how its history of political violence affects your practice and to think about your role in joined-up health and social care in a society after conflict.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work students and social workers in Northern Ireland
statements.about: registration and the assessed year in Northern Ireland
statements.paraphrase: Since 2004 an honours degree in Social Work is the recognised qualification there for social workers, for probation officers and for education welfare officers; since protection of title in 2005 every student and qualified social worker is required to register with the Social Care Council, and graduates register on condition of an Assessed Year in Employment.

forPractitioner.text: In Northern Ireland, students must register with the Social Care Council, honours is the professional qualification, and new graduates are registered on condition that they complete an Assessed Year in Employment.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study in Northern Ireland, you must register with the Social Care Council as a student, and once you graduate your registration depends on completing an assessed first year in work.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work students in Scotland
statements.about: the qualifying award and SSSC registration in Scotland
statements.paraphrase: The SSSC approves all qualifying courses, keeps registers, sets codes and regulates training; practising in Scotland needs a recognised qualification and SSSC registration, and to qualify professionally students must gain a generic Social Work honours degree or a postgraduate award of equal standing.

forPractitioner.text: In Scotland, to qualify, students must hold a generic Social Work honours degree or a postgraduate award of equal standing, and practice needs SSSC registration; courses work to the SSSC's revised standards and requirements.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study in Scotland, to qualify you must gain a generic Social Work honours degree or a postgraduate award of equal standing, and you will need to register with the SSSC to practise.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: students progressing through a course
statements.about: progression through levels to the threshold skills
statements.paraphrase: Across an honours degree (FHEQ 6; SCQF 10) or an integrated master's (FHEQ 7; SCQF 11), students move from level to level under each institution's rules; each level is expected to build towards meeting the threshold subject and generic skills, usually with credit gained for all learning and assessment, practice included.

forPractitioner.text: Design each level so that it builds towards the threshold subject-specific and generic skills, and expect students to complete and gain credit for every element, practice components included.

forBeneficiary.text: As you move from one level of your course to the next, each stage builds towards the minimum skills you need by the end, and you will usually need to pass everything, including your practice learning.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: all Social Work routes
statements.about: practice learning integrated into every route
statements.paraphrase: Social work can be taken as a BA or BSc, a postgraduate conversion, a PgDip, an MSc, MSci or MA, or a degree apprenticeship, and every one of these routes will build in practice learning so students can use and grow their skills in real situations.

forPractitioner.text: Whatever the route, from BA to MA or apprenticeship, build practice learning into the programme so that students apply and develop their skills in real situations.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on course design; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: students of the subject
statements.about: applying ethics to oneself and judging others
statements.paraphrase: Ethics, social justice and professional values sit at the centre of design, with activities that carry values into research, practice and daily conduct; students will be able to bring this to bear on their own values and behaviour and to judge critically how others behave ethically.

forPractitioner.text: Build activities that apply values and ethics to research, practice and conduct; students will be able to apply them to their own value base and critically evaluate the ethical conduct of others.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to apply social work values and ethics to your own beliefs and behaviour, and to judge critically how ethically other people act.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses
statements.about: partnership with people with lived experience
statements.paraphrase: Courses are expected to work alongside people with lived or living experience to build understanding, empathy and good practice, so students hear many perspectives, test their assumptions and reflect more widely.

forPractitioner.text: Partner with people who have lived or living experience so that students hear a wide range of voices, question their own perceptions and reflect more broadly.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: an expectation of the course; the student meets its effect

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses and practice partners
statements.about: written practice agreements and stakeholder views in design
statements.paraphrase: Courses partner with practice learning providers and stakeholders; practice-based learning will rest on a written agreement among practice educators, supervisors, course and placement providers and students, and courses are expected to bring in the views of employers, practitioners and those with lived experience when designing and reviewing the curriculum.

forPractitioner.text: Put every practice placement under a written collaborative agreement among all parties, and bring employers', practitioners' and lived experience views into curriculum design, development and review.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on the course and its partners; the student is a party to the agreement but the duty is the course's

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses
statements.about: alignment with the relevant regulator's standards
statements.paraphrase: Courses should be written to align with the standards of the regulator in the nation where they run.

forPractitioner.text: Write the course so that it lines up with the standards of the regulator for the nation where it is delivered.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on course design

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: providers
statements.about: external reviewers in periodic review
statements.paraphrase: Externality is essential to UK quality assurance: providers will bring in external reviewers in periodic review for an independent view of proposed changes and to make sure threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: Include external reviewers in periodic review to test proposed changes independently and confirm threshold standards and subject content.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Social Work course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses
statements.about: regulatory approval and ongoing monitoring
statements.paraphrase: Courses will need regulators' approval and continuing monitoring, usually through a mix of visits and desk review.

forPractitioner.text: Expect regulatory approval and continued monitoring of the course, normally by site visits combined with desk-based review.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on the course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses
statements.about: principles for course content
statements.paraphrase: Providers design at set levels using the national frameworks of their nation; content is expected to be relevant, up to date, evidence informed, current and coherent, and co-production, responsiveness and inclusive, decolonised content are welcomed.

forPractitioner.text: Base content on relevance, currency, evidence and coherence; design at the right framework level for your nation; co-produce with stakeholders where you can and make content inclusive and decolonised.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: an expectation of the course

statements.appliesTo: students and courses
statements.about: practice-based learning and integration of knowledge into practice
statements.paraphrase: Practical learning is fundamental: in work settings it means taking part directly with people with lived experience, families, carers, communities and other professionals, alongside observation, shadowing, supervision, reflection and research, and knowledge is expected to be clearly integrated into practice.

forPractitioner.text: Make practice learning central, with direct work alongside people with lived experience and professionals, and expect students to show clearly how they bring knowledge into practice.

forBeneficiary.text: Learning in practice is a core part of your course: you will work directly with people and other professionals, and you are expected to show clearly how you put what you know into practice.

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses
statements.about: scaffolded teaching and a range of facilitators
statements.paraphrase: Teaching is staged, starting with induction and orientation at each level, students take more responsibility as they progress, and learning is expected to be led by a range of people, including academics, researchers, practitioners and people with lived experience.

forPractitioner.text: Scaffold teaching from induction onward, hand students more responsibility over time, and involve academics, researchers, practitioners and people with lived experience in facilitating learning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: an expectation of the course

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses
statements.about: assessment principles and readiness for practice
statements.paraphrase: Assessment rests on inclusion, accessibility and integrity and will build in feedback and feed forward; it measures learning, checks professional standards and supports reflection, with clear criteria linked to outcomes, and it judges readiness for practice, progress and the final award.

forPractitioner.text: Ground assessment in inclusion, accessibility and integrity, build in feedback and feed forward, link criteria to outcomes and use assessment to judge readiness and fitness for practice.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on the course's assessment

statements.appliesTo: Social Work students and graduates
statements.about: academic and practice requirements, and regulators' standards
statements.paraphrase: Social work is a professional qualification at undergraduate or postgraduate level; students must show they have met both the academic and the practice requirements of their course, and graduates are also expected to meet any standards of the regulator in their nation.

forPractitioner.text: Assess both academic and practice requirements, since students must show they meet both; graduates also face the national regulator's own standards.

forBeneficiary.text: You must show that you have met both the academic and the practice requirements of your course, and you will also be expected to meet the standards of the regulator in the nation where you study.

statements.appliesTo: providers developing competence standards
statements.about: threshold standards are not competence standards
statements.paraphrase: The minimum threshold standards are not meant as universal competence standards; a provider that sets competence standards under equality law may draw on the statement and PSRB requirements, and in that case should follow the latest Equality and Human Rights Commission guidance.

forPractitioner.text: Do not treat the threshold standards as competence standards in the equality-law sense; if you write competence standards, follow the latest EHRC guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider

statements.appliesTo: Social Work courses
statements.about: academic level 6 or 7 and regulator outcomes
statements.paraphrase: Practice requirements are the same across undergraduate and postgraduate routes, but academic study will be designed and assessed at the right level, 6 (SCQF 10) or 7 (SCQF 11); every degree is accredited by a regulator, whose outcomes for registration will also apply.

forPractitioner.text: Keep practice requirements common across routes while pitching academic modules at Level 6 (SCQF 10) or Level 7 (SCQF 11), and apply the regulator's learning outcomes for registration as well.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a requirement on course design

statements.appliesTo: providers classifying awards
statements.about: classes above threshold follow the provider's marking schemes
statements.paraphrase: Integrated master's degrees use similar classes (2:2, 2:1 and first), master's degrees give merit and distinction above the threshold, and for every award the criteria above threshold will follow the provider's common or generic marking schemes.

forPractitioner.text: Classify achievement above the threshold through your institution's common or generic marking schemes, for every award covered.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a provider duty in classification

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates
statements.about: at least threshold across four categories
statements.paraphrase: Honours graduates in Social Work must show at least threshold attainment in every category of four areas: what they know and understand, the skills they show, values and ethics, and PSRB requirements.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure every honours graduate reaches at least the threshold in all four areas: knowledge and understanding, skills, values and ethics, and the regulator's requirements.

forBeneficiary.text: To gain your honours degree you must reach at least the minimum standard in all four areas: what you know and understand, the skills you show, your values and ethics, and the regulator's requirements.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: providers and regulators
statements.about: threshold criteria and practice days
statements.paraphrase: Threshold criteria will follow the provider's common or generic undergraduate marking schemes and the sector standards used in each UK nation, and the regulator will also set the threshold, including the required number of mandatory practice days.

forPractitioner.text: Set threshold criteria in line with your undergraduate marking scheme and the sector standards of your nation, and take the number of practice days from the regulator.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a provider and regulator matter

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: social work's role worldwide and across the UK nations
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown an awareness of what social work does internationally, in the UK and in each of the four UK nations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown awareness of the profession's role internationally, across the UK and within each of its four nations.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you know what social work does around the world, across the UK and in each of the four UK nations.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: difficult decisions, including restricting liberty
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to take and carry out hard decisions, liberty-restricting ones included, in human situations that may bring benefit while understanding the harm involved.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the capacity to make and carry out difficult decisions, including those that restrict liberty, weighing possible benefit against harm.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you can make and carry out hard decisions, including ones that limit someone's freedom, while weighing up the good and the harm they may do.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: social work across the sectors
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown an understanding of how social work operates in statutory, independent and voluntary bodies and the wider third sector.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown understanding of how the profession works in statutory, independent and voluntary organisations and the third sector.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you understand how social work is done in statutory services, independent and voluntary organisations and the third sector.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: defending decisions with evidence
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to defend decisions with confidence, using a broad range of evidence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the capacity to justify decisions confidently on a wide evidence base.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you can explain and defend your decisions confidently, using a wide range of evidence.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: research as the evidence base for practice
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the ability to find, judge and critically use research so that professional practice rests on sound evidence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the ability to locate, appraise and critically apply research so that it grounds and steers practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you can find research, judge how good it is and use it critically so your practice rests on sound evidence.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: leadership and advocacy
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to show professional leadership and skill in advocacy.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the capacity to show professional leadership and advocacy skills.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you can show leadership as a professional and speak up for the people you work with.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: theory, policy, law, methods and skills in practice
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown a critical understanding of theory, policy, the legal framework, methods and skills, and of how each bears on practice.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown critical understanding of theory, policy, law, methods and skills, and of how each applies in practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you understand theory, policy, the law, methods and skills critically, and see how each one shapes what you do in practice.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: professional boundaries
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to keep professional boundaries, stay within the limits of the role and find support when needed.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the capacity to hold professional boundaries, work within the role's limits and identify support where needed.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you keep professional boundaries, stay within the limits of your role and know where to get support when you need it.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: consistent, reflective use of social work skills and methods
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown consistent use of social work skills and reflective use of a range of methods, grounded in critical thinking, decisions informed by evidence and an understanding of varied practice settings, across items n to hh.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown a consistent use of social work skills and a reflective use of varied methods, resting on critical thinking, evidence-based decisions and understanding of different practice settings, as items n to hh set out.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you use social work skills consistently and choose and reflect on a range of methods, thinking critically and basing decisions on evidence.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: the regulators' required knowledge, skills and behaviours
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown evidence of the knowledge, skills, broader behaviours or professional competences that the regulators require.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown evidence of the knowledge, skills, behaviours or competences that the relevant regulator requires.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown evidence that you have the knowledge, skills and professional behaviours your regulator asks for.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: critical reflection on performance
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to reflect critically on one's own performance, drawing on feedback and evidence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the capacity to reflect critically on their own performance using feedback and evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you can reflect critically on how you are doing, using feedback and evidence.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: current debates on inequality, power and oppression
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown engagement with current cultural and social debates, for instance about inequality, power and oppression.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown engagement with present-day cultural and social debates, inequality, power and oppression among them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you engage with today's cultural and social debates, for example about inequality, power and oppression.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: continuing professional development
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to take part in continuing professional development, spotting gaps in knowledge and how to close them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the capacity to pursue continuing professional development, identifying knowledge gaps and how to address them.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you keep developing as a professional, noticing gaps in what you know and finding ways to fill them.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: climate and environmental justice and social work's part
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown an understanding of why climate change, environmental and social justice, conflict and weakening democracy matter, of social work's part in meeting their effects on people and communities, and of how environmental harm and its threat to human rights fall hardest on those already facing poverty, racism, ableism or other disadvantage.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown understanding of why climate change, environmental and social justice, conflict and democratic decline matter to the profession, of its role in responding to their effects, and of how environmental harm lands hardest on those already disadvantaged.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you understand why climate change, environmental and social justice, conflict and threats to democracy matter for social work, what social workers can do about their effects, and why environmental harm hits people already facing poverty, racism or ableism hardest.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: support and supervision
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to make good use of support and supervision so that practice stays safe, effective, accountable and sustainable under heavy demands.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the capacity to use support and supervision well, keeping practice safe, effective, accountable and sustainable under pressure.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you make good use of support and supervision so that your work stays safe, effective, accountable and sustainable when the pressure is on.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: need and risk
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the ability to recognise and make sense of need and risk and to respond to them fittingly.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the ability to understand, identify and respond appropriately to need and risk.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you can recognise need and risk, make sense of them and respond in the right way.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: own wellbeing
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the capacity to take responsibility for one's own wellbeing, acting appropriately and seeking support.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown the capacity to take responsibility for their own wellbeing, acting appropriately and seeking support.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you look after your own wellbeing, taking sensible action and asking for support when you need it.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: intersecting factors in need and risk
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown recognition of how overlapping parts of identity and disadvantage can shape need and risk, with the ability to respond and to challenge when needed.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown recognition of intersecting factors that bear on need and risk, and the ability to respond and challenge where required.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you can see how different parts of someone's identity and situation combine to affect need and risk, and that you respond and challenge when you need to.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: knowledge base and values across disciplines
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown an understanding of the profession's knowledge base and values and of how to apply them together when working with other disciplines.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown understanding of social work's knowledge and values and how to use them together in interdisciplinary work.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you understand what social work knows and values, and how to use both together when you work with other professions.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: contested contexts and a commitment against oppression
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown critical awareness of disputed political and social contexts, with a commitment to practice that opposes discrimination, oppression and racism.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown critical awareness of contested political and social contexts and a commitment to practice that challenges discrimination, oppression and racism.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown that you are critically aware of disputed political and social contexts and committed to practice that stands against discrimination, oppression and racism.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: joined-up knowledge of the profession's context, knowledge base and its use
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown a joined-up knowledge and understanding of where professional social work takes place, of what the profession knows and of how that knowledge is used, across items a to m.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates will have shown a coherent grasp of the setting of professional social work, of its knowledge base and of how that knowledge is applied, as items a to m set out.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for your honours degree, you will have shown a joined-up grasp of where social work happens, what the profession knows and how that knowledge is used in practice.

headingPath: Bachelor's degree with honours: Minimum standards

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject at threshold
statements.about: relating to people with lived experience and professionals
